title: Murphy Sign and Acute Cholecystitis: Interpretation Limits
subject: Eponyms
preview: Murphy sign is inspiratory arrest with pain during right upper quadrant palpation.
quickRevision: Murphy sign is inspiratory arrest with pain during right upper quadrant palpation.
Ultrasound findings, systemic inflammation and a compatible symptom pattern improve interpretation.
A negative Murphy sign can occur in older patients or severe disease; consider the whole clinical picture.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Murphy sign is inspiratory arrest with pain during right upper quadrant palpation.
A positive sign can support acute cholecystitis but is not diagnostic in isolation.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Ultrasound findings, systemic inflammation and a compatible symptom pattern improve interpretation.
A negative Murphy sign can occur in older patients or severe disease; consider the whole clinical picture.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not confuse Murphy sign with Charcot triad, which suggests cholangitis.
